comparison: Both address claims C36-C43 regarding DSK-expressing neurons (MP1 and Sv) identified via anti-FLRFa antibody. OpenEval finds the immunohistochemical data fully supported by genetic rescue. Peer review raises significant concerns about antibody specificity, requesting DSK-specific antibody validation and noting this as a study weakness, resulting in UNCERTAIN evaluation versus OpenEval's SUPPORTED.

Both address claims C56-C61 regarding calcium imaging showing CCKLR-17D1 function in Goro neurons. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance (p<0.05-0.01) and appropriate controls. Peer review accepts the calcium imaging data as supporting CCKLR-17D1's functional role without concerns.

Both address claims C62-C71 regarding anatomical characterization of MP1 and Sv neurons with descending projections. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights single-cell labeling and marker studies. Peer review explicitly accepts the anatomical demonstration of brain-to-VNC projections without critique.

Both address claims C72-C75 regarding CaMPARI2 imaging showing no heat-evoked activation but tonic activity in MP1 neurons. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the tonic activity interpretation is appropriately speculative. Peer review accepts this interpretation and frames it as raising interesting questions for future study.

Both address claims C99-C103 regarding hypotheses about MP1 tonic activity and activation mechanisms. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are appropriately presented as speculation lacking direct evidence. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the tonic activity hypothesis as an interesting direction for future research rather than a weakness.

Both address claims C108-C111 regarding additional DSK signaling pathways beyond the MP1-Goro circuit. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes differential CCKLR-17D3 effects support additional pathways requiring future identification. Peer review accepts these observations without concerns.

Both address thermogenetic activation experiments (C81-C86, with R8 also including C87). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with significant statistical results. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 raising critical concerns that the experiment doesn't clearly address whether activating DSK neurons suppresses acute heat nociception, requesting additional dTRPA1 experiments.

Both address claims C89-C91 regarding acute modulation versus developmental effects. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes morphological analysis and functional data distinguishing from NMJ effects. Peer review accepts this distinction between developmental and physiological roles without concerns.

Both address claims C93-C98 regarding IPC neurons not being involved in DSK-mediated nociception. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites immunohistochemical and CaMPARI2 data supporting IPC irrelevance. Peer review accepts this conclusion without raising concerns about the IPC analysis.

Both address behavioral phenotypes of dsk mutants. OpenEval R2 covers C3-C4, C25-C28 (basic mutant phenotype and rescue). Peer R1 covers these plus C31-C34 (temperature specificity). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and genetic rescue. Peer review notes all three reviewers explicitly affirm findings with 'conclusive genetic experiments' and 'clean logic.'

Both address receptor localization and function in Goro neurons (C49-C54, with R3 also including C44-C47). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes RNAi/rescue experiments with appropriate controls. Peer review explicitly accepts receptor localization and functional experiments without concerns.

Both address connectivity between MP1 and Goro neurons. OpenEval R10 covers C76-C80 (anatomical proximity and connectivity assays). Peer R7 covers these plus C104-C107 (volume transmission interpretation). Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights negative synaptic assays suggesting non-synaptic communication. Peer review accepts the interpretation of bulk peptidergic transmission based on careful experiments.

OpenEval R17 addresses claims C104-C107 regarding volume transmission mechanism, rated SUPPORTED as appropriate inference. Peer R7 addresses these same claims along with connectivity data (C76-C80), also SUPPORTED. Both accept the volume transmission interpretation based on negative synaptic connectivity results.

Both address the major conclusion about descending inhibitory pathway. OpenEval R13 covers C6, C10, C17, C113, C115 emphasizing comprehensive evidence and evolutionary speculation. Peer R9 covers C5-C7, C87, C113, C115. Both are SUPPORTED. All peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'convincing,' 'conclusive,' and 'exceptional' demonstration of descending pathway in non-mammalian organisms.

OpenEval R3 addresses claims C29, C31-C34 regarding temperature-specific thermal hypersensitivity at 42°C but not 38°C, rated SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes these claims (C31-C34) along with basic mutant phenotypes (C3-C4, C25-C28), also SUPPORTED. Both accept the behavioral data demonstrating temperature specificity.

OpenEval R5 addresses claims C44-C48 regarding receptor expression patterns, rated SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C44-C47 along with functional data (C49-C54), also SUPPORTED. Both accept the receptor localization data showing widespread CNS expression and specific patterns in Goro neurons.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C5, C87 as central conclusion supported by convergent evidence, rated SUPPORTED. Peer R9 addresses these along with C6-C7, C113, C115 regarding the descending pathway conclusion, also SUPPORTED. Both strongly affirm the major finding with comprehensive experimental support.

OpenEval R12 addresses C5, C87 as central conclusion, rated SUPPORTED. Peer R8 addresses C81-C87 focusing on thermogenetic activation experiments, rated UNCERTAIN due to concerns about experimental design. Overlap is minimal (C87 only), with peer review questioning the strength of functional demonstration that OpenEval accepts.

OpenEval R1 addresses claims C1-C2, C15-C16, C18, C30, C35 regarding neuropeptide homology and CCK system conservation, rated SUPPORTED based on established literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.

OpenEval R19 addresses claims C8-C9, C11-C14, C19-C23 as background knowledge supported by established literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims about pain mechanisms and nociception.

OpenEval R20 addresses claims C112, C114, C116-C120 as discussion points about broader implications and potential impacts, rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these forward-looking discussion claims.
